newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast raises palm oil price, sells assets.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast raises palm oil price, sells assets.

text.p: Ivory Coast has raised its producer price for palm oil in the 1996/97 season from 26 CFA francs per kg to 31.5 CFA, a cabinet statement said.
The statement, read on state television on Saturday, said the government had approved the increase on the recommendation of the price fixing committee and operators in the industry.

At Friday's cabinet meeting, President Henri Konan Bedie also signed decrees authorising the sale of more segments of the state's Palmindustrie agro-industrial giant, which has been divided up for privatisation.
The Societe Africaine de Financement et de Participation (SAFIPAR) is to take a 70 percent stake in the Anguededou-Dabo-Eloka unit in the centre-east, the statement said.
Ivorian company PALMCI will take a 70 percent stake in the Ehania-Toumanguie unit in the southeast and an unspecified stake in the central Irobo-Boubo unit.
